extraction.name: MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark
extraction.description: A benchmark for evaluating text embedding models across 8 tasks and 58 datasets covering 112 languages, with open-source code and a public leaderboard.
extraction.creator: Niklas Muennighoff, Nouamane Tazi, Loïc Magne, Nils Reimers
extraction.rai:dataCollection: MTEB datasets were assembled from a variety of existing public datasets and sources, including public APIs (arXiv and bioRxiv/medRxiv), Reddit posts, StackExchange posts, Amazon reviews, Twitter datasets, Kaggle competitions, BUCC, Tatoeba, SemEval, BEIR, and other publicly available benchmarks.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web API, Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Public datasets and corpora from arXiv, bioRxiv/medRxiv, Reddit, StackExchange, Amazon customer reviews, Twitter, Kaggle competitions, BUCC, Tatoeba, SemEval, BEIR, and other publicly available benchmark datasets.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For arXiv clustering datasets, titles and abstracts were concatenated for P2P inputs; for S2S inputs only titles were used. For bioRxiv/medRxiv, title and abstract were concatenated for P2P inputs and only titles were used for S2S inputs. For arXiv, when multiple categories were available for a paper, only the first category was used. For some datasets, MTEB created custom splits and sampled subsets of labels/articles.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Datasets were organized into S2S, P2P, and S2P settings; some tasks used train/dev/test splits as provided, while others used only test or dev splits. For evaluation, the paper states that all datasets except MSMARCO used test splits, and MSMARCO used the dev split. Some datasets were filtered into subsets of labels and sampled to create splits of varying size.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were taken from the source datasets when available. For clustering datasets, cluster labels were generated from human-assigned paper categories. For bitext mining datasets, annotated sentence pairs correspond to translations. For reranking datasets, manual annotations marked question pairs as similar or dissimilar. For classification datasets, labels came from the original dataset annotations (e.g., intents, sentiment, toxicity).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper notes that for arXiv clustering, multiple categories may exist and only the first category was used. It also notes that some datasets rely on the same corpora and that overlap with model training data was ignored in MTEB scores because controlling for contamination was challenging.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: MTEB is open-source and versioned at both dataset and software levels. Results are published as JSON files on the Hugging Face Hub, and the benchmark includes a public leaderboard with automatic submission support. Community contributions via pull requests are welcomed.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The benchmark includes multilingual data covering 112 languages and datasets involving geography/language-related variation; some source datasets include user comments, reviews, tweets, and banking queries. No explicit collection of sensitive human attributes is described.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to improve evaluation of text embedding models across diverse tasks and languages, helping practitioners select appropriate models and reducing blind reuse of models across tasks.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes task imbalance across the benchmark, multilingual coverage concentrated in some tasks, and potential contamination from overlap between benchmark datasets and model training data. It also notes that retrieval and clustering are English-only.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Very long documents are missing; summarization is represented by only one dataset; retrieval and clustering are English-only; code datasets are absent; and benchmark averages may be biased toward tasks with many datasets. The paper also notes that overlap with model training data is not controlled for in scores.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation of text embedding models across classification, clustering, pair classification, reranking, retrieval, semantic textual similarity, summarization, and bitext mining. The benchmark is used for testing and comparative evaluation of models, not for training or fine-tuning.
